skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with overly broad activation wording, but no hidden code, persistence, credential handling, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly favors local-hardware-friendly outputs such as scripts, templates, checklists, and small-model or CPU-safe workflows, and does not request broad filesystem, network, credential, or account access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains markdown and YAML files only, with no executable scripts, installers, package hooks, or command-running instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger keywords and examples are broad, including generic terms like security, gate, every, must, and before, so accidental invocation is plausible, but the runtime instructions themselves are ordinary planning and artifact-generation guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, credential/session/profile access, or data indexing behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to help users produce workflows, checklists, analyses, and implementation support for SkillScan-style security and reliability work; the artifact content matches that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should know this skill may activate too often because its trigger wording is broad. It is otherwise a low-risk documentation workflow helper; consider narrowing the trigger keywords or invoking it explicitly by name when needed.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The scanner's routing concern is supported by artifact text: the manifest, trigger lists, examples, and implicit invocation metadata use broad terms that could match unrelated requests. I treat this as a real activation-quality issue, but not enough for Review because the artifacts do not add high-impact authority, hidden behavior, data access, or automatic mutation.
